chapter: Clarinet teachers and the Baton Rouge scene
title: Reading music and what Manuel Roque taught
summary: Some bands read, Toots did not; Roque taught him waltzes, scales and simple tunes, more than Picou ever did, with Fritz giving free lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Those early bands, when they called it Ragtime, were they reading bands?
Oh, no. Certainly not. A lot of them couldn't read. But Manuel could read, my teacher. Toots I don't think read.

I had to have a book to start with. He taught me the waltz, and he taught me the scales, and things like that, and the simple tunes to play. In fact, he taught me more than Picou ever taught me. Now, that's the only teacher I ever had in Baton Rouge, was Manuel Roque, and Isadore Fritz(?) would come around and give me a few lessons for free.
